newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-COETZER SLAMS DOOR ON GRAF -- AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COETZER SLAMS DOOR ON GRAF -- AGAIN.

text.p: South Africa's Amanda Coetzer ended Steffi Graf's grand slam title hopes for the second time this year when she knocked the defending champion out of the French Open quarter-finals on Tuesday.

World number two Graf, who had reached the final at Roland Garros eight times in the last 10 years, found herself swept aside 6-1 6-4 by the opponent who humiliated her 6-0 6-1 in Berlin last month and dispatched her from the Australian Open in January.
"I could sense she lacked confidence," Coetzer said. "But I can understand that.
"She's been injured and hasn't played much and I've had a couple of wins over her, so I know I would feel the same way."

Having missed three months of tennis earlier this year with tendinitis in her left knee, Graf was in trouble right from her opening serve as Coetzer broke her twice in the first set to jump out to a 4-0 lead.

At the other end of the court, Coetzer, the 11th seed, was unspectacular but steady, giving nothing away against her 27-year-old opponent who was guilty of numerous uncharacteristic unforced errors, 29 in the first set alone.

Trailing 2-0 in the second set, Graf finally broke Coetzer and appeared ready to get back into the match only for the South African to break back immediately to keep the pressure on the increasingly frustrated German before play was suspended because of rain.

Graf, winner of the last two French Opens, did her best to stage a comeback following the 30-minute delay but ultimately slid to her first defeat in Paris since losing in the 1994 semifinals to Mary Pierce.
"It was a difficult match, I was really nervous and made a lot of mistakes," Graf, five times French Open champion, said.
"It's just the state I'm in, I just don't seem to have the confidence against her. I've struggled in all my matches here but I was always able to turn them around. That wasn't the case today."
Coetzer will meet Iva Majoli in the semifinals and Graf, for one, does not fancy the diminutive South African's chances of advancing to the final over her 19-year-old Croatian opponent.
"Probably not," said Graf when asked if she expected to see Coetzer in Saturday's final. "She's playing with confidence and steady but to win the tournament would be difficult for her."

Majoli, the ninth seed, earned her first appearance in a grand slam semifinal after struggling to a 6-3 5-7 6-2 win over her doubles partner Ruxandra Dragomir in a gruelling match which took two hours and 23 minutes to complete.
Quarter-finalist for the last two years at Roland Garros, Majoli led 5-3 in the second set but squandered three match points, allowing the Romanian to force a third set.

Majoili did not make the same mistake again, finally converting her fifth match point before collapsing on to the red clay where she was joined by Dragomir, who clambered over the net and fell to the ground giggling beside her.

"It's hard to play your doubles partner and friend," said Majoli, who also disposed of Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport on her way to her to the last four. "We were both so exhausted, I had to lay down, I couldn't walk anymore.
"She came over to my side and it was a nice feeling that we could still be the same after this kind of match."
Majoli, however, had none of those same warm feelings for French Open officials who scheduled her match and all three other women's quarter-finals on an outside court.
"I wish we had played this match on Centre Court, we have great quarter-finals and deserve to be on Centre Court," she said. "I think this was a Centre Court match and so are the other three matches.
"We're not happy, we deserve to be equal to the men and play on Centre Court from the quarter-finals until the end of the tournament."
